back_translation: The burden-oracle concerning Tyre: Wail, O ships of Tarshish! For Tyre has been devastated, with neither house nor harbor left. The news reached them from the land of Kittim.
Be struck silent, O inhabitants of the coastland, and you merchants of Sidon, whom the seafarers who cross the sea have made abundantly rich.
Across the great waters came the grain of Shihor; the harvest of the Nile was her revenue, and she became the marketplace of the nations.
Be ashamed, O Sidon, for the sea has spoken; the fortress of the sea says: "I have never been in labor and never given birth; I have never raised young men nor brought up young women."
When the news reaches Egypt, they will writhe in anguish at the report about Tyre.
Cross over to Tarshish; wail, O inhabitants of the coastland!
Is this your city of revelry, the city so ancient from days of old, whose feet once carried her to settle in far-off lands?
Who planned this against Tyre, the city that bestows crowns, whose traders are princes, whose merchants are the honored ones of the earth?
The LORD of Hosts planned it — to defile the pride of all glorious beauty, to bring low all the honored ones of the earth.
Till your land like the Nile valley, O Daughter of Tarshish, for there is no longer a harbor binding you.
He has stretched out His hand over the sea; He has made kingdoms tremble. The LORD has given a command concerning Canaan, to destroy all its strongholds.
He said: "You will revel no more, O crushed Virgin Daughter of Sidon. Rise, cross over to Kittim — even there you will find no rest."

Look at the land of the Chaldeans — this people is no longer of any account — Assyria destined it for desert creatures. They erected siege towers, stripped its palaces bare, and turned it into a heap of ruins.
Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for your fortress has been destroyed!
In that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the span of a single king's reign. At the end of the seventy years, Tyre will be like the song of the prostitute:
"Take up the lyre, walk about the city, O forgotten prostitute. Play sweetly, sing many songs, so that you will be remembered again."
And at the end of seventy years, the LORD will visit Tyre. Then she will return to her hire and will prostitute herself with all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth.

But her merchandise and her wages will be set apart as holy to the LORD; they will not be stored up or hoarded, for her merchandise will go to those who dwell before the LORD, for abundant food and fine clothing.
